source_read: https://timhortons.co.uk/information/<id> (all 277 product and size pages, fresh download 2026-10-08, robots.txt allows all) and the Nutrition PDF https://timhortons.co.uk/assets/img/products/Nutrition-20261008-151007-ece8.pdf ('C5 - 8.10.26 v7', created 8 Oct 2026, fresh download)
notes: All 253 rows (244 published + 9 already held back) compared two independent ways: my own HTML parse of every page (9 nutrients, kJ, serving, weight, vegetarian, page 'Allergens:' line) and my own pdftotext parse of the PDF's nutrition and allergen tables (all 253 rows, Yes and Maybe cells, 'Suitable for Vegetarians'), plus rendered PDF pages 3 and 11 read by eye: 0 differences in nutrition or contains marks. Live drift: BLT Chicken Wrap changed since 6 Oct (394 -> 445 kcal, 182 -> 224 g; PDF v7 agrees) so data/source was rebuilt from the fresh pages. Extraction omission fixed in tim_hortons.py: the PDF prints 'Maybe' (= may contain) for 126 rows (e.g. Mocha wheat, Frappes nuts/soya/wheat, all donuts) but allergen_guide said may_contain_published 'no' and no may-contain was carried; now carried (policy 2 applied where a key is in both columns), flag set to yes. Also: PDF version stamp regex now reads 'C5 - 8.10.26 v7'; Honey Dip Timbits prints 100 kJ with 57 kcal (kcal agrees with its macros and %RI, kJ is the outlier): dish kept, kJ left unpublished for that row (policy 1; kj_conflicts in the script). The 9 existing hold-backs re-confirmed. Allergens and tags were first written for this chain in this run (data/source had none).
